contract.configuration: Canonical allowed_projects IDs must be enrolled. project:<id> owner implies its exact singleton project; conflicting/arbitrary owner labels are rejected. Empty allowed_projects explicitly means host administrator-only global use.
contract.cas: Definition upsert/trust/delete bind to the current nonsecret definition_digest. Credential changes rotate a nonsecret credential_revision even if the binding name is unchanged.
contract.credentials: Write-only set_mcp_credential supports bounded stdio env, HTTP/SSE header and OAuth client-secret bindings. Only backend-derived MCP references/configured booleans return; credentials never enter canonical native configuration events.
contract.direct_tools: Connect/call require current agent-run including trusted_execution/project grants. Project scope and approved catalog/tool names are checked before RPC and before response publication. Live definition edits invalidate pooled access until explicit reconnect.
contract.internal: The existing Internal ToolRegistry/scheduler/approval loop exposes mcp_catalog and mcp_call. Dispatch freezes actual definition/catalog digests and preset connection/tool selection; every effect validates owned active task, exact originating SID/principal/policy, authorized execution project/cwd and live delegated grant. Unknown external effects require normal action approval.
contract.native: Project-scoped direct MCP bindings fail closed before resolving credentials because current native integrations do not prove mandatory per-MCP-call revocation interception. Global administrator bindings retain their declared trusted boundary; changed definition/scope cannot silently reuse a native session.
contract.runners: Host MCP credentials/connections never transfer to a dedicated runner; incompatible preset selection fails before provider dispatch.
contract.lifecycle: Each pooled SDK connection holds its async cancellation scopes inside one persistent owning task; disconnect shuts down that task across independent HTTP request tasks.

limits: MCP project scope binds the invocation to an authorized execution project. An external MCP service owns its own tool semantics; this does not advertise hostile-tenant OS isolation for arbitrary server commands.
Global native MCP is an explicit administrator trust boundary. Per-tool project-scoped native integration remains unsupported rather than silently dropping current scope checks.
No paid provider call, personal credential mutation, installer GUI or enterprise MCP deployment is inferred from controlled source fixtures.
